createdBy: T-025 plan round 1 (self-audit under RULES.md L-006)
impact:
BLOCKED ON ISS-082, WHICH MUST BE ANSWERED FIRST. Plan review round 3 established that this issue's central term - "per-source" - is undefined, and that the answer changes this issue's conclusion rather than merely informing it. sourceVersion is Record<string, number> and nothing binds the key domain (see ISS-082). Read that first; what follows is correct only once "source" means something.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED REGARDLESS OF ISS-082. The only per-entity ccusage surface, `claude daily --instances` (src/ccusage.ts:68-78), is DAY-granular: rows carry `date`, `totalCost`, `totalTokens`, four optional counters, `modelBreakdowns` (src/json.ts:327-331). Generic `daily` uses `period`, same granularity. A day-granular watermark does not advance within a day, so if the key domain resolves to projects or instances, then no intra-day refresh can ever publish - defeating T-012's fast tier and the product - and N-008 1b would report "found nothing new" for a run that found real new spend, which is the exact freshness lie 1b exists to prevent.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. That no per-source sub-day signal exists. `ccusage blocks --json` (src/ccusage.ts:96) rows carry `startTime`, `endTime` and `actualEndTime` as ISO instants with ms precision (tests/fake_ccusage.py:67-70), consumed at renderers.ts:397-399, reached by the live `blocks` subcommand (main.ts:70,122,146). The rows have no source key, but the COMMAND is Claude-only - so under provider-level keys that timestamp IS a per-source sub-day signal for Claude, and this issue narrows to Codex. Under project-level keys it is global and this issue stands at full width. Codex `sessionFile` (ROLLOUT_RE, codex.ts:59-62) embeds a time but it is a session START time, which a growing session never advances, so it does not witness newest activity under any key domain.

HISTORY OF THIS FILING, kept because the pattern matters more than the conclusion. Version 1 claimed "no row in any ccusage surface carries a sub-day event timestamp" - FALSE, refuted by review round 2, which found blocks. Version 2 claimed "no PER-SOURCE sub-day signal exists" - NOT ESTABLISHED, refuted by review round 3, which found that the term was undefined. Both times the error was the same: I audited what I was already looking at, found what I expected, and stopped. ISS-072 was withdrawn for that pattern earlier in this arc. That is three instances, and the lesson is not "check ccusage surfaces" but "an audit that terminates when it finds a confirming instance has not been performed".

CANDIDATE RESOLUTIONS, once ISS-082 is answered:
(a) Ordered composite per-source version, e.g. (newest day, tokens on that newest day) - monotone and pruning-robust, since pruning never touches the newest day. Costs: sourceVersion is Record<string, number>, so the pair needs a checked safe-integer encoding, or the type and compareSourceVersions both change on shipped T-010. Splitting across two keys does NOT work: at day rollover the date component rises while the token component resets, giving anyGreater && anyLess = incomparable (dominance.ts:184).
(b) Keep day-granular watermarks and REDEFINE "unchanged" as candidate-payload-identical-to-live rather than watermark-equal, letting an equal watermark with a differing payload publish. Weakens the gate to refusing only regression.
(c) Accept day-granular publishing for v0.2 and move intra-day freshness to the v0.5 owned-parsing ticket - i.e. state plainly that the v0.2 service updates spend once per day.
(d) Per-source day watermarks plus the global blocks.actualEndTime as an intra-day tiebreak. WITHDRAWN AS PROPOSED, and the reason is worth keeping: review round 3 showed it commits this arc's own substitution. To claim the payload REFLECTS activity through blocks.actualEndTime, blocks must be invoked BEFORE the payload-producing command; invoked after, it proves only that blocks SAW activity, not that the computed payload included it - bytes-available-as-bytes-consumed wearing a new hat, inside the fix proposed for it. It was also underspecified on persistence, regression handling, interaction with retirement and equality, and invocation order, and it cannot unblock a growing Codex session when the Claude tiebreak is unchanged. Revivable only with a strict `blocks` -> payload ordering contract and a full composite comparison table.

If ISS-082 resolves to PROVIDER keys, a fifth option opens: Claude uses blocks.actualEndTime as a genuine per-source sub-day watermark while Codex uses day granularity, with the asymmetry documented rather than hidden. That is the option this issue could not see while "source" was undefined.
title: No ccusage surface gives a PER-SOURCE sub-day activity time: a per-source watermark cannot advance intra-day, and the only sub-day signals are global or session-start
